transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-11-17
Start: 14:05 PT
Duration: ~52 minutes (recording)
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Jonas Ruiz (Redwood SE), Priya Malhotra (Cedar Head of ML), Eric Lawson (Cedar Platform), Sara Lim (Cedar Product)

Summary (auto): quick walkthrough of Redwood Console's prompt health / eval monitoring features (prompt sets, regression alerts, A/B comparison). Customer wants low-friction pilot for monitoring LLM regressions across model pinning and rollout A/B. Discussed data residency, KMS, and performance tradeoffs for hosted vs private. Next steps agreed.

Topics: Prompt sets, regression alerting thresholds, A/B comparison dashboards, exportable evals, onboarding pilot, security questions (SOC2, KMS), integration with CI/CD for model rollouts.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — Maya from Redwood, I'll kick off and then hand to Jonas for the demo. 
[00:18] Priya: Hey, thanks. We got about an hour, um, so excited to see the monitoring side — we've built a big prompt library and want to catch regressions early.
[00:28] Jonas: Great, that's exactly what today's demo is about — we'll show prompt sets, how to baseline expected outputs, the regression alerts, and then the A/B compare UI for rollouts.
[00:38] Eric: Quick one — we care about data never leaving our VPC, like really private. Is this a hosted-only feature?
[00:46] Maya: Short answer: the Console features work across Hosted and Dedicated; for Private we can push the same Control Plane configurations. Jonas, correct me if I misstate anything.
[00:55] Jonas: Yep, Console is UI/control plane agnostic — prompt set definitions and eval jobs can run in your dedicated pool or private deployment. For the pilot we usually start hosted to move fast then flip to a VPC flow if you need KMS/HSM.
[01:10] Sara: And audit logs? We need per-prompt auditability for compliance.
[01:14] Jonas: Console keeps an immutable eval history and you can export audit bundles. There's also token-level cost traces if you need chargebacks.
[01:23] Priya: Sweet. Can we jump into the demo?
[01:27] Jonas: Yep. I'm sharing my screen — apologies if the network is a bit choppy.
[01:34] [screen share begins] Jonas: Here's the Console home, top-left is 'Optimize' suggestions, but we'll go into 'Prompt Health' module.
[01:44] Maya: Note: sometimes our share names get munged in transcription, you might see K V cache written funny.
[01:50] Jonas: Right, so first thing — prompt sets. You can create a set and attach multiple prompts, expected outputs, and a rubric. For Cedar we'd recommend 3 tiers: smoke tests, business-critical prompts, and random-sample quality checks.
[02:06] Priya: For the rubric, can we use pairwise scoring? We want to capture subtle ranking differences.
[02:11] Jonas: Absolutely. The eval engine supports pairwise, scalar scoring, and custom prompts for automated checks. Pairwise is useful for UI-based A/B where you surface a winner.
[02:20] Eric: How are baselines computed? Like do you run a 7-day baseline or a one-off?
[02:25] Jonas: You can configure baseline windows — typical is a rolling 7-30 day baseline. We compute metrics like BLEU-ish similarity, embedding distance, and a custom business rubric score.
[02:36] Sara: Does that include embedding drift? We saw a model update once that moved embedding space and broke rerankers.
[02:42] Jonas: Yes, we track embedding centroid shifts and expose drift alerts. You can set thresholds and have automatic regression alerts trigger.
[02:49] Priya: Show the actual alert configuration for us?
[02:52] Jonas: Sure — here's an alert config. You can set trigger conditions like >8% drop in rubric score, >0.12 embedding distance shift, or a percentile drop for top-k accuracy. You can chain conditions too.
[03:05] Priya: Uh-huh. Can those alerts call our incident system? PagerDuty?
[03:09] Jonas: Yes, webhook, PagerDuty, Slack — we also emit structured events for your observability backend.
[03:17] Eric: Does the alerting run in-line or as a downstream job? I'm thinking about resource usage.
[03:22] Jonas: It's a scheduled eval job that runs on your selected pool; can be lightweight (sample-based) for low cost or full-grid for thoroughness. For Dedicated we recommend nightly full-grid runs in off-peak windows.
[03:34] [05:00 mark — jump in transcript for brevity]
[05:02] Jonas: Now A/B compare — when you rollout a new model/version you can configure an A/B split and Redwood will automatically compute paired evaluations between variant A and B against the same prompt set.
[05:15] Priya: That paired comparison — is it deterministic? We want to avoid randomness confounding the metric.
[05:19] Jonas: We seed requests and cache prefixes so the test harness is deterministic given the same random seed. Also you can pin temperature and sampling params for the run.
[05:30] Sara: Can we do per-route rollouts, like 10% traffic to new model only for chat route?
[05:34] Maya: Yes, per-route and per-customer policy routing — you can route by model tag, region, or customer tier.
[05:40] Eric: A practical question — if we want to pilot, what's the small footprint path? We don't want to spin up a ton of infra for the first two weeks.
[05:47] Maya: Typical pilot: hosted API with dedicated eval jobs, you feed us 3 prompt sets and a baseline sample, we run nightly evals and alert you. If results look good, move to dedicated or private.
[05:59] Priya: Do you capture and persist the KV cache data? We have long multi-turn prompts.
[06:04] Jonas: We surface KV cache usage metrics but do not persist user KV by default — that lives in your runtime. For private deployments you control retention.
[06:12] [07:30] Jonas: I'm now clicking into a sample prompt set from a demo tenant — note this has both human-labeled expected outputs and automated rubric functions. See the 'delta' column showing percent negative regressions over last week.
[07:43] Priya: I see a spike on Nov 10 — what caused that?
[07:46] Jonas: Looks like a model variant update — we can drill down to the exact prompt examples that regressed.
[07:53] Maya: (interrupting) Quick aside: sometimes our transcript shows weird product names — like 'Redroot' — ignore that.
[07:59] Priya: Ha, noted.
[08:02] Jonas: Back to the UI — clicking example one shows original expected response and actual response with token-level diff highlighting. You can flag examples to add to your 'must-pass' set.
[08:16] Sara: Can we export that diff to a CSV for internal review?
[08:19] Jonas: Yep, exports include the prompt, baseline response, actual response, rubric scores, and embedding vectors if you want them.
[08:27] Eric: About data residency again — if we do hosted how are the embeddings stored and encrypted?
[08:33] Jonas: In hosted we encrypt at rest with provider keys but we also support customer-managed KMS for Dedicated and Private. We can include a KMS diagram in the security pack.
[08:43] Priya: Can you run the evals against an older pinned model? We sometimes want to compare against model X-2.
[08:49] Jonas: Absolutely — the eval config lets you select any model version in the catalog or a pinned artifact from your private registry.
[08:56] [10:00ish] Jonas: Now I'll show the A/B results page — we show side-by-side metric summaries, pairwise win rates, and an explainability overlay that surfaces prompt-level drivers of regressions.
[10:12] Priya: Explainability overlay — is that using attention or feature importances?
[10:16] Jonas: We use a mix: token saliency heuristics plus embedding similarity and an attribution layer for the scoring rubric. It's not a formal model explainability paper, but it's actionable.
[10:26] Sara: How do you handle false positives? We don't want alerts every time literally a punctuation change happens.
[10:32] Jonas: Two levers: change thresholds, and a 'noise-tolerant' mode that ignores minor token diffs under a length-normalized threshold. Also you can set a required consecutive failure count before alerting.
[10:46] Priya: Nice. Any rate limits on eval runs?
[10:50] Jonas: Depends on plan — hosted has per-account evaluation quotas but they're adjustable for pilot accounts. Dedicated/private you manage the compute.
[10:58] Eric: We use in-house inference for some sensitive functions — can Redwood integrate the eval runner against our endpoints?
[11:04] Jonas: Yes, we can configure the eval runner to call your endpoints via a secure connection (short-lived certificates or VPC peering). We treat it like any model endpoint.
[11:12] [13:00 marker jump]
[13:05] Jonas: One neat feature we use internally — the 'eval change composer' where you can batch a set of prompt fixes and rescore to see projected impact before shipping.
[13:16] Priya: That would help product triage. Do you have an API to trigger those rescores in CI?
[13:20] Jonas: There's a REST API and SDKs — you can programmatically kick off eval jobs, pull results, and gate deployments based on thresholds in CI.
[13:29] Sara: So we could block a rollout if pairwise win-rate < 70%?
[13:33] Jonas: Exactly, you can define a gating policy.
[13:36] Eric: Who typically owns the prompt sets on your side vs ours?
[13:40] Maya: Customer owns canonical prompt sets; Redwood's SE can help curate and seed typical rubrics. For pilots we often co-maintain until ownership transfers.
[13:49] Priya: Security question again — SSO/SAML?
[13:52] Maya: Yes, SAML SSO integration is available, RBAC roles map to Console sections, and audit logs export to your SIEM.
[13:59] [15:00] Priya: Can you show a sample regression alert email?
[15:04] Jonas: Opening an example — it lists failing prompts, delta scores, link to the A/B run, and suggested rollback.
[15:12] Priya: Suggested rollback — can Redwood automatically rollback traffic?
[15:16] Jonas: We have an automatic fallback policy that will shift traffic to a pinned stable model if a critical alert fires. You can set thresholds for automatic vs manual intervention.
[15:28] Eric: That could save us nights.
[15:31] Maya: Agreed.
[15:33] [18:00 jump]
[18:05] Jonas: Quick note on cost: Optimize will give batching and quantization suggestions per model and workload; for evals we recommend sampling to save tokens and run full evals less frequently.
[18:17] Priya: Does Optimize recommend quantization levels that might change model quality? We're sensitive to quality drops.
[18:23] Jonas: It will simulate expected quality delta and show estimated latency/cost savings so you can trade off. You can also run the eval suite on the quantized variant to verify.
[18:34] Sara: Do we get a single dashboard per route showing both live latencies and eval regressions?
[18:39] Jonas: Yes, per-route dashboards aggregate live SLOs and eval metrics; we also provide a combined view for correlation.
[18:46] Priya: Perfect.
[18:48] [21:00 jump]
[21:05] Maya: Quick cadence question — how often do customers keep evals running?
[21:10] Jonas: Most do lightweight smoke evals hourly and full evals nightly, with weekly full cohort runs for longer-term drift analysis.
[21:20] Eric: Any recommended sample sizes?
[21:23] Jonas: For smoke tests 200-500 prompts; for full grid 5k-20k depending on surface area.
[21:30] Priya: Great. Will you send us a recommended prompt sampling strategy?
[21:33] Maya: Yes — Jonas will include that in the runbook.
[21:37] [28:00 jump]
[28:02] Jonas: I'm going to demonstrate a recent regression case — here's a product that did A/B over Thanksgiving and the A variant had a 12% drop in business rubric. You can see the top contributing prompts and the recommended mitigation: pin older model for the affected cohort and fix two prompts.
[28:21] Priya: How easy is it to pin an older model for only a subset of customers?
[28:26] Jonas: It's a policy rule — you can set client tags, and route by tag. For example: if customer.org == 'internal', use model v1.2 else v1.4.
[28:38] Sara: What about RBAC for who can trigger rollbacks?
[28:42] Maya: RBAC roles control model rollout privileges; we recommend only ops and SRE have rollback permissions.
[28:49] Eric: We also want logging of who triggered what — is that in audit?
[28:53] Jonas: Yes, every rollout change is an auditable event with user id and timestamp.
[28:58] [34:00 jump]
[34:03] Priya: Real question — how do you measure the UX impact vs metric deltas? Sometimes a small metric drift doesn't matter.
[34:09] Jonas: We support custom business metrics and human-in-the-loop sampling: you can tag prompts that are UX-critical and require human review for any negative regression above the guardrail.
[34:21] Priya: Could we have product own those tags?
[34:24] Maya: Yes, product defines the taxonomy.
[34:26] Sara: Do you support multi-language prompt sets? We need English and Japanese.
[34:31] Jonas: Yes, multilingual evals are first-class — you can tag language and compare across locales.
[34:40] [40:00 jump]
[40:06] Maya: Quick pricing note — pilot is typically waived or heavily discounted and we include security docs for enterprise prospects.
[40:14] Priya: That's helpful.
[40:16] Eric: Any caveats on running eval jobs in hosted with PII?
[40:20] Jonas: Don't send raw PII to hosted unless you've executed the right agreements; for pilot we recommend sanitized samples or run in Dedicated/Private with KMS.
[40:29] Priya: We'll sanitize initial sets.
[40:31] Maya: Great.
[40:33] [46:00 jump]
[46:05] Jonas: Final demo bit — the A/B report export. You can embed that into CI as a JSON payload and the gating checks run as part of your deploy pipeline.
[46:16] Priya: That's exactly what we wanted.
[46:19] Sara: Any gotchas when integrating with our existing model registry?
[46:22] Jonas: We integrate with common registries and you can also upload model artifact references; for air-gapped setups we support a push model.
[46:30] Priya: Great.
[46:32] Maya: Okay let's recap next steps — Maya to send pricing and security bundle, Jonas to send runbook and example prompt sampling strategy, Priya to share canonical prompt lists and SLTs, and we'll schedule a pilot kickoff.
[46:46] Priya: Sounds good.
[46:48] Eric: One last small ask — can Jonas include an abridged 'how we handle KV cache' note?
[46:53] Jonas: Yup — I'll add that to the runbook.
[46:57] Maya: Okay, thanks everyone — we'll follow up in email.
[47:02] Priya: Thanks, bye.
[47:05] Sara: Bye.
[47:07] [call ends]

Notes on transcription quality: medium — speaker labels sometimes overlap and a few technical terms transcribed oddly (K V cache, Redroot).

References shared: demo deck link (internal), sample prompt set CSV (uploaded to shared drive), security pack (attached to follow up email).

End of transcript.
